title: Proof-point definition and load checklist sync
next_steps: Redwood to share benchmark spreadsheet, runbook, and load scripts by 2026-10-15
BlueArc to provide 3-day sample traffic trace and sample PII-redacted corpus by 2026-10-18
Schedule live benchmark window (2 hours) for week of 2026-10-26 — tentative: 2026-10-27 09:00 PT
Security to review KMS/HSM key policy and provide gaps by 2026-10-21
action_items: Jordan Lee: Deliver benchmark template + example results; due: 2026-10-15
Priya Nair: Prepare two load profiles (conversational baseline and high-concurrency stress) and attach runner configs; due: 2026-10-16
Samir Gupta: Draft acceptance-checklist with threshold table (p50/p95 latency, accuracy delta, error rate); due: 2026-10-15
Maya Chen: Supply sample traffic distribution and a 3-day anonymized corpus; due: 2026-10-18
Carlos Rivera: Confirm VPC peering window and network egress limits for benchmark window; due: 2026-10-20
Nadia Patel: Provide compliance/retention constraints and must-have audit logs; due: 2026-10-21
summary: Kickoff to lock down the POC proof-points: performance thresholds (p50/p95), throughput targets, reporting format and who supplies artifacts. Agreed on two load profiles and a 2-hour live benchmark run. Redwood to provide benchmark kit; customer to supply traces and compliance requirements.
topics: Success criteria table: latency, throughput, accuracy delta, error budget
Workload sizing: concurrency, token distribution, sequence lengths
Benchmark mechanics: runner, VM/GPU type, quantization, caching
Timeline and windows for live runs
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-10-12 14:00 PT -> 52m. Attendees noted.

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — quick roll call?
[00:06] Maya Chen: Maya here, hi.
[00:08] Carlos Rivera: Carlos.
[00:10] Nadia Patel: Nadia.
[00:12] Ellen Brooks: Ellen here.
[00:14] Priya Nair: Priya from Redwood, hi!
[00:17] Jordan Lee: Cool, thanks. Objective today is pretty narrow — define the proof-points for the POC and the load/run checklist so we can run the live benchmarks next week or the week after.

[02:05] Maya Chen: High level from our side: we want to validate two things — latency under typical conversational load and then that cost/throughput numbers make sense at scale. Also need to prove that private deployment meets our data controls.

[03:20] Jordan Lee: Great. We'll try to split into criteria, inputs we need from BlueArc, and then the run mechanics. Priya, Samir you want to take the perf knobs?

[03:32] Priya Nair: Yeah. For criteria we're proposing a small table: p50 latency target < 120 ms for short-turn responses (<=64 tokens), p95 < 250 ms, error rate < 1% (timeouts/5xx), and quality delta < 3% measured on our eval set. Those are configurable but we need baseline.

[04:10] Maya Chen: 3% quality delta — that's BLEU-ish? how are we measuring?

[04:20] Samir Gupta: Good question. We'll use the evaluation harness you already have or our lightweight accuracy checks: a set of 200 golden prompts and expected output similarity — we can do rubric-based scoring or embedding-similarity; we'll include both. We should define acceptance threshold as "no more than 3% drop on embedding-similarity and manual spot-check failures <= 5 out of 200".

[05:05] Nadia Patel: On security: we need to ensure keys never leave our KMS, audit logs for every request, and optional on-prem deployment if network egress is blocked. We need to see the audit log schema.

[06:00] Jordan Lee: We'll attach our logs schema in the runbook. For the KMS, private Redwood private mode supports customer-managed KMS/HSM — we'll note steps.

[06:40] Carlos Rivera: From infra sizing: our traffic is spiky. Baseline is 120 req/s average with peaks to 650 req/s for ~10 minutes. Sequence lengths vary — 70% short (<=64 tokens), 25% medium (65-256), and 5% long (>256). Tokenization is BPE-ish, average tokens per request ~48.

[07:20] Priya Nair: Perfect. We'll generate two runner profiles: "conv-baseline" (120 rps sustained, small bursts) and "stress-high-peaks" (simulate 650 rps peaks, concurrent connections up to 450). We'll also provide suggestion for batch sizes — e.g., continuous batching targeting latency SLOs.

[08:10] Ellen Brooks: Is the plan to run against your hosted endpoint or dedicated pool? We prefer dedicated to mirror production.

[08:22] Samir Gupta: For fidelity we recommend Dedicated (A100 or H100 depending on model). If customer can't provide dedicated, we can run hosted variant but we'll call that "lower fidelity". Dedicated helps ensure consistent throughput and predictable quantization path.

[09:00] Maya Chen: We have a capex constraint — we might start with a hosted session to validate functionality then move to dedicated. Want to see both numbers side-by-side.

[09:18] Jordan Lee: We'll include a dual-run plan: one quick hosted smoke run, and the main dedicated run. The benchmark sheet will have columns for both.

[10:00] Carlos Rivera: Network: our VPC peering requires a maintenance window. We'll need to confirm peering date; otherwise we can test via temporary secure tunnel. I'll follow up with a date.

[11:05] Nadia Patel: Also need to confirm log retention windows and who has access — SOC 2 requires retention of 12 months for request-level audit. We'll flag anything less as non-starter.

[11:30] Priya Nair: Noted — runbook will include audit log retention and role-based access controls. We'll flag if additional retention is needed.

[13:20] Jordan Lee: Let's get into the acceptance-test format: we propose a simple artifact: a one-page "result tile" per run with: run id, config (model/quant/instance), workload profile, p50/p95 latencies, throughput (tokens/s and reqs/s), error rate, quality delta, and pass/fail per-row.

[14:05] Maya Chen: That sounds actionable. We need a single pass/fail rubric at the top: if p95 exceeds target by >10% or quality delta >3% or error rate >1.5% -> fail. Is that reasonable?

[14:30] Samir Gupta: Yes. Let's define exact thresholds in the table. Example: p50 target 120 ms (fail if >132 ms), p95 target 250 ms (fail if >275 ms), error rate threshold 1% (fail if >1.5%), quality delta 3% (fail if >4%). We can allow a minor exceedance but we should capture severity.

[15:20] Maya Chen: We might want a soft-fail category so we don't kill the POC on a single hiccup — e.g., if failure is due to batching misconfiguration or cold-starts.

[15:40] Jordan Lee: Agreed. We'll add result tags: PASS, MARGINAL, FAIL and include notes for root-cause. Marginal requires remediation plan and a re-run within 3 business days.

[16:25] Carlos Rivera: For report format — CSV + human-readable PDF summary works for us. Also want raw logs (compressed) and the runner trace.

[17:00] Priya Nair: We'll publish a Git-style artifact: CSV metrics, compressed request logs, runner config, and a short analysis PDF. We'll also include a per-token cost estimate (approx) for the run.

[18:10] Ellen Brooks: Cost estimate helpful. Provide both: spot cost (current run) and projected cost for our expected monthly throughput.

[19:00] Samir Gupta: We'll model cost for several quantization options and cached vs uncached scenarios. Note: prefix caching can reduce token cost and latency for repeat sequences.

[19:45] Maya Chen: Quick question on quantization — we saw different behavior on 4-bit vs 8-bit; will you support the same model weights for both?

[20:05] Priya Nair: Typically yes, there's a quantized variant; runtime selects kernel paths. We'll state which quantization profile used in the run artifact. Some differences in quality are expected — that'll appear in the quality delta column.

[21:12] Jordan Lee: Back to timeline. We want the live dedicated run in the week of 2026-10-26. Customer to confirm maintenance window for VPC peering by 2026-10-20. Is that okay?

[21:30] Carlos Rivera: I'll try for the 20th. If not possible, we can do a tunnel test.

[22:05] Nadia Patel: On compliance evidence: we need proof of SOC 2 Type II and the ability for us to extract audit logs per request ID. Can you provide a sample request log schema?

[22:40] Jordan Lee: Yes, in the runbook. We'll send sample logs and the schema.

[23:20] Maya Chen: For acceptance, who signs off? Myself + Carlos + Nadia?

[23:32] Ellen Brooks: Product sign-off should include PM, infra, and security — so Maya, Carlos, Nadia, Ellen.

[24:00] Jordan Lee: Good. We'll include a sign-off table at the end of the report where those names sign digitally or via email confirmation.

[25:10] Priya Nair: A few technical notes: the runner will capture both token-level timings and end-to-end latency. We'll surface p50/p95 with 95% CI if we run multiple iterations. We'll also capture cold-start counts.

[26:40] Samir Gupta: For reproducibility, we'll pin model version and seed. We'll also record model artifacts and quant flags. That way any re-run uses exact config.

[27:55] Maya Chen: If the dedicated pool uses different instance types, will results transfer?

[28:05] Priya Nair: We'll include an "equivalence" note — dedicated results are primary. If you run on different instance types we will annotate expected delta.

[29:30] Carlos Rivera: For long tail and memory issues — we need an upper bound on KV cache usage and OOM rates.

[29:45] Samir Gupta: We'll instrument OOMs and memory headroom; pipeline will abort runs that exceed a configured OOM threshold and flag as fail.

[31:00] Jordan Lee: Let's walk through an example row in the acceptance table so everyone's clear. Samir?

[31:05] Samir Gupta: Sure. Run id: RA-20261027-01; Model: redwood-rw-70B-fp16; Instance: 4xA100-80GB; Workload: conv-baseline; p50: 98 ms; p95: 210 ms; throughput: 350 req/s; tokens/s: 28k; error rate: 0.4%; quality delta: 1.2%; Pass status: PASS. Notes: caching enabled, quantization none.

[32:10] Maya Chen: That example looks good. What if we see high p95 due to token-bloat from certain prompts?

[32:28] Priya Nair: We'll capture request histograms and top offenders. The report will include a "top 10 slowest prompts" with counts. That helps you triage prompt-level issues.

[33:10] Ellen Brooks: Regarding reporting cadence — send initial artifacts within 24 hours of run, and a final consolidated report within 3 business days.

[33:25] Jordan Lee: That's our standard. We'll stick to 24 hours for raw artifacts and 72 hours for the final report.

[34:40] Maya Chen: One more ask: can we get a simple CSV that maps run ids to cost-per-million-tokens so finance can sanity check?

[34:52] Samir Gupta: Yes — cost column included in the CSV. We'll show both realized cost and projected monthly cost based on your throughput profile.

[36:10] Nadia Patel: If we decide to move to private on-prem later, will the same acceptance artifact work?

[36:20] Priya Nair: Mostly yes. On-prem introduces different network constraints and often different hardware; we'll note that but keep the same pass/fail criteria with host-specific annotations.

[37:35] Carlos Rivera: For the runner tech: is it a JMeter-based harness or something custom?

[37:45] Priya Nair: It's a custom runner built on k6 and a lightweight orchestration so we can replay traces precisely and attach token timings. We'll share the repo link.

[38:20] Jordan Lee: Ok let's summarize the acceptance thresholds we agreed: p50 < 120 ms, p95 < 250 ms, error rate < 1%, quality delta < 3%, with PASS/MARGINAL/FAIL bands as discussed and re-run rules.

[39:02] Maya Chen: Confirmed. Also, include a marginal ruleset so we can triage.

[39:20] Samir Gupta: We'll add a marginal band (p95 10-20% over target or error rate 1-1.5% or quality delta 3-4%) and remediation guidance.

[40:55] Ellen Brooks: Timeline recap?

[41:00] Jordan Lee: Deliverables: benchmark kit by 2026-10-15, customer artifacts by 2026-10-18, live run week of 2026-10-26, preliminary artifacts within 24h, final report within 72h.

[41:30] Carlos Rivera: I'll aim to lock peering by 2026-10-20.

[42:10] Maya Chen: Security will review the logs schema once we get it.

[43:00] Nadia Patel: We'll also send a short list of legal/compliance questions; keep an eye out for an email.

[44:18] Jordan Lee: Quick note on metrics — we'll include both absolute numbers and normalized per-1k tokens so you can compare across models.

[44:40] Priya Nair: We'll also output a single-page executive summary for your procurement — includes cost and recommended next steps.

[45:30] Maya Chen: One operational ask: if we see a marginal result, how fast can Redwood remediate and re-run?

[45:42] Samir Gupta: For small config issues we can triage same day and schedule re-run within 48-72 hours; for infra changes it might take longer, we'll note in the remediation plan.

[46:30] Ellen Brooks: Any red flags from your side?

[46:34] Priya Nair: Nothing blocker — just dependencies: sample traffic and peering window. Once those are in place the plan is straightforward.

[47:12] Jordan Lee: All right, let's confirm sign-off owners: Maya, Carlos, Nadia, Ellen. Redwood owner Jordan. We'll put a sign-off table in the report.

[47:40] Maya Chen: Sounds good.

[48:05] Carlos Rivera: I'll send the exact VPC window and constraints by 2026-10-20.

[48:30] Nadia Patel: I'll send compliance constraints and the list of minimum audit fields.

[49:00] Jordan Lee: We'll deliver the runbook and benchmark kit by 2026-10-15. Expect an email with attachments.

[50:10] Priya Nair: One last thing — we'll flag any known model caveats in the run artifact (e.g., certain token sequences that cause longer decode times).

[50:42] Ellen Brooks: Appreciate it.

[51:10] Jordan Lee: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the artifact and calendars — meeting adjourned.

End of transcript.
